messages:
olivia.sr: Quick sync on the FinservX POC — they want an enterprise commit with a preheat window and a clear hedging plan for spot/evict fallback. Need a throughput sizing + autoscale handoff and a ballpark monthly cost for the execs. @sanjay.ml can you size GPUs? @evan.infra can you propose autoscale + AZ hedge?

sanjay.ml: Sure. A few quick Qs: what's their expected steady RPS and peak burst RPS? token/prompt P95 or target seq lengths? model family? latency SLO (p95 generate time)? Also, are we serving chat streams (multi-turn) or single-shot generation?

olivia.sr: Customer answered in questionnaire — pasted below:
```
profile: {
  peak_qps: 180,    # peaks during business hours
  steady_qps: 60,
  mean_tokens_per_req: 320,
  p95_tokens: 900,
  chat_rate: 70%,
  latency_slo_p95: 600ms
}
model_preference: llama-3-70b-quant (8-bit) for quality; willing to accept a quantized variant for tail latency
preheat_window: 30m before peak
availability: multi-AZ, HIPAA-adjacent workload
```

sanjay.ml: Thanks. Quick back-of-envelope: assume 900 tokens at p95, and we target 600ms p95. For an optimized runtime on A100-like class with quantized 70B, one GPU can sustain roughly ~25-40 p95 requests/min depending on batching and KV cache effectiveness. Converting their peak 180 QPS -> 10.8k req/min. So naive GPU count = 10,800 / 40 = 270 GPUs (wild overestimate if naive). But with batching, KV cache, and request shaping (chat locality + prefix caching) we can reduce that dramatically.

sanjay.ml: Realistic plan: - Use model warm KV cache and session affinity for chat -> expect 4–6x improvement in effective throughput. - Autoscale base to cover steady QPS (60 qps) with smaller footprint, and reserve a committed pool to cover 95th-percentile predictable load. My recommendation: reserved pool = 20 GPUs (for consistent throughput and SLA) + burst pool (autoscale) up to 120 GPUs in the region for peak. That gives headroom while keeping most capacity reserved for sustained traffic.

ev an.infra: For autoscale + hedge: propose two pool types: reserved (committed) and burst (spot/ephemeral). Policies:
- reserved min_replicas = 20 (no scale-down below this for SLA)
- burst_pool_max = 120
- scale_up_policy: step scale by 10 GPUs when queue depth > 2000 tokens equivalent for 30s
- scale_down_cooldown: 10m after last high queue event
- preheat job: a controlled warmup that runs KV-warmup traffic for 15–30m before predicted peak window
- AZ spread: place reserved replicas across at least 3 AZs; burst can be AZ-local to minimize cross-AZ egress costs and degrade gracefully on AZ failure
Note: spot fallback should have an eviction policy that drains in-flight sessions to reserved pool and falls back to smaller model variant if evictions spike.

marta.ops: On pricing: rough monthly estimate for committed + burst design. Using ballpark on-prem-equivalent pricing: reserved 20 GPUs @ $8k/GPU-month => $160k/mo. Assume average burst usage of 40 GPUs for 6 hours/day across 22 business days -> ~40 * 6 * 22 = 5280 GPU-hours (~220 GPU-months equivalent) charged at burst rate $1.8k/GPU-month = ~ $396k amortized. Total rough monthly cost footprint ~ $560k. We usually propose a blended commit discount (example: 20 reserved + committed burst credits) -> suggest presenting a 25% blended discount to keep effective ARR competitive.

sanjay.ml: A couple of technical caveats to share with the customer:
- KV cache warmup can be done via synthetic replay of recent prefixes; expect a short period (5–15% latency penalty) while caches populate.
- Quantized 8-bit variants reduce memory + throughput needs but may increase latency variance; keep a fallback smaller model for spot evacuations.
- For chat-heavy workload, session affinity (sticky routing) is essential to leverage KV cache.

olivia.sr: Legal/security asks: they submitted a security questionnaire asking about KMS, audit logs, SOC2, and on-prem options. Can we confirm Private supports customer-managed KMS + VPC access + audit trails? I can send the PDF.

ev an.infra: Yes: Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM integrations, VPC-only control plane, and audit logs with S3 retention. For hosted Dedicated we can enable KMS key wrapping and VPC peering. We'll attach an ops-runbook section covering key rotation and incident play for evictions.

olivia.sr: Next steps: 1) Sanjay to produce a compact sizing note with two scenarios (conservative and optimized with KV warmup) including GPU counts and expected p95 latency. 2) Evan to produce autoscale + AZ fallback policy snippet and a short ops-runbook for preheat. 3) Marta to draft initial pricing proposal with blended discount and burst credit structure. 4) I'll send the security questionnaire and schedule a 30m sync with the customer next Tue.

sanjay.ml: I'll drop the sizing note by EOD tomorrow with numbers and the assumptions table. Quick sample calc I'll include: tokens/sec = qps * tokens_per_req -> 180 * 900 = 162k tokens/sec at peak. If optimized pipeline yields ~2k tokens/sec per GPU for target latency, that implies ~81 GPUs peak; with 4x cache/batching gains -> ~20 GPUs reserved + burst to 100–120.

deploy-bot: [deploy bot] scheduled: runbook-template:v2 applied to sales/presales/finservx at 2026-03-23T15:42:01Z

olivia.sr: Great — thanks all. I'll ping customer that we have a firm plan and share the EOD sizing. If anyone wants to prep any diagrams (AZ layout, failover flow), add them to the runbook thread. :thumbsup:
